explanation.expected_timing_gain: Significant reduction in combinational delay; typically 50-70% shorter mapped path (from seven adder delays down to about three logic levels plus one final 16-bit adder).
explanation.bottleneck: The baseline creates all partial products but then sums them with a serial chain of seven 16-bit carry-propagate additions. Each adder waits for the previous sum, so the critical path grows linearly with the number of rows.
explanation.functional_boundaries: No changes to module name, port widths, unsigned semantics, or timing contract. All 2^16 input combinations produce the same 16-bit product.
explanation.rewrite: Replace the explicit serial accumulate with the single synthesizable multiplication operator. Synthesis tools infer a parallel carry-save partial-product reduction tree (Wallace/Dadda) followed by one final carry-propagate adder, reducing the dependency depth from O(N) to O(log N).
explanation.area_or_other_cost: Area remains comparable; the synthesis tool can balance the parallel CSAs. Minor area increase possible relative to the smallest serial design, but controllable via synthesis constraints.
